title: Chemical bonds, ionic, covalent and metallic

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Noble gas electronic structure
items.clue: The full outer shell arrangement of a Group 0 element.

items.label: Alloy
items.clue: A mixture containing a metal and one or more other elements.

items.label: Covalent bonding
items.clue: Bonding in which the particles are atoms which share pairs of electrons.

items.label: Metallic bonding
items.clue: Bonding in which the particles are atoms which share delocalised electrons.

questions.stem: The specification describes covalent bonding in terms of which particles?

options.text: ions which have swapped electron pairs
atoms sharing delocalised electrons
atoms which share pairs of electrons
electrons moving from atom to atom

questions.explanation: This is the specification's wording: for covalent bonding the particles are atoms which share pairs of electrons.

questions.stem: How are the atoms arranged in a pure metal?

options.text: in a giant structure with a regular pattern
randomly, in a closely packed jumble of atoms
a lattice of positive and negative ions
in small groups of a few joined atoms

questions.explanation: The specification states that metals consist of giant structures of atoms arranged in a regular pattern.

questions.stem: Which of these is a compound held together by ionic bonding?

options.text: lithium fluoride, a metal and a non-metal
sulfur dioxide, a compound of two elements
hydrogen chloride, a gas containing chloride
nitrogen gas, an element with very strong bonds

questions.explanation: Lithium is a metal and fluorine a non-metal, which is exactly the condition the specification gives for ionic bonding.

questions.stem: Which statement about the electrons in a metal is correct?

options.text: each atom keeps its outer electrons, loosely
every electron in every atom is delocalised
the outer electrons are free to move about
the electrons are transferred to the ions

questions.explanation: The electrons in the outer shell of metal atoms are delocalised and so are free to move through the whole structure.

questions.stem: Covalent bonding occurs in which of these?

options.text: compounds of non-metals only, never in elements
any compound made from two different elements
non-metals combined with metals in a lattice
most non-metallic elements and non-metal compounds

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: covalent bonding occurs in most non-metallic elements and in compounds of non-metals.

questions.stem: What gives rise to the strong metallic bonds in copper?

options.text: attraction between metal ions and delocalised electrons
attraction between positive and negative ions
shared pairs of electrons between two metal atoms
each atom holding on to its own outer electrons

questions.explanation: The sharing of delocalised electrons gives strong metallic bonds: the positive metal ions are attracted to the electrons.

questions.stem: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc. Which type of bonding does it have?

options.text: ionic, because it contains two different elements
metallic, because alloys bond like pure metals
ionic, since positive ions attract negative ions
covalent, as the atoms share outer electrons

questions.explanation: The specification states that metallic bonding occurs in metallic elements and alloys.

questions.stem: In terms of electrostatic forces, what is the ionic bond in sodium chloride?

options.text: attraction between oppositely charged ions
the movement of an electron across the bond
a pair of electrons shared by the ions
attraction between the two atomic nuclei

questions.explanation: Chemical bonding is explained by electrostatic forces; in an ionic compound these act between the positive and negative ions.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly links the three bond types to what happens to the outer electrons?

options.text: ionic and metallic share electrons; covalent transfers
all three types involve sharing pairs of electrons
ionic transfers electrons; covalent and metallic share them
covalent shares electrons; ionic and metallic do not

questions.explanation: Ionic bonding transfers electrons, covalent bonding shares pairs between atoms and metallic bonding shares delocalised electrons.

questions.stem: In terms of electrostatic forces, what is a covalent bond?

options.text: attraction between the shared pair and both nuclei
attraction between the two positive nuclei
attraction between ions and delocalised electrons
an electron moving from one atom to the other

questions.explanation: The shared pair of electrons is attracted to the nuclei of both bonded atoms, and that attraction is the bond.
